A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iMOOE research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE forecasting experiments, SST evaluation, ablations, and appendix experiments on pendulum dynamics, 3D fluids, and time series.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds sea-surface elevation forecasting, irregular-grid Airfoil experiments, and additional ablation results.

M1.justification: The original architecture and training objectives remain unchanged. However, the new Airfoil extension in Appendix F.2.4 calculates spatial derivatives using finite elements and discards the FFT-based frequency loss, introducing a limited procedural adaptation for irregular grids.

E1.justification: v2 adds measured sea-surface elevation dynamics alongside SST and introduces Airfoil forecasting on irregular triangular meshes, jointly predicting velocity, density, and pressure. These additions substantially extend the represented physical dynamics and spatial-domain conditions; the earlier datasets remain.

E2.justification: Geo-FNO becomes an evaluated comparator in the new Airfoil comparison, alongside previously evaluated VCNeF and OFormer (v2 Table 17). Original comparator sets remain unchanged. SSE reuses the SST comparator set rather than introducing additional baseline methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include SSE's chronological 4000/500-frame split and four-input/six-output forecasting, plus Airfoil's 1000/100 sequences and four-input/22-output forecasting with nMSE and RMSE. The partition ablation adds a time-only control. These extend evaluation without revising the original benchmark settings.

E4.justification: The frequency-loss ablation expands from DR to SST and SSE, including frequency-band errors (v2 Table 8). The environment-partition study adds time-only grouping to the retained parameter-only and combined controls (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 11). These are targeted extensions of existing analyses.

E5.justification: Existing mean/standard-deviation displays and runtime uncertainty reporting are retained. The new SSE table follows the existing reporting format; neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: Matched original numerical results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial benchmark and ablation evidence. SSE Table 5 reports iMOOE nMSE 1.52e-2 versus DPOT's 2.46e-2. Airfoil Table 17 reports OFormer nMSE 4.95e-2 without iMOOE versus 4.14e-2 with it. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance improvements between versions under an existing setting.

T1.justification: New Appendix B argues that iMOOE satisfies the structure of a cited operator universal-approximation theorem by matching its local and nonlocal modules. This adds a limited approximation argument; the original invariance definitions and equations remain unchanged, and no new OOD generalization theorem or full proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: two-level PDE invariance, the operator-expert architecture, frequency-enriched invariant learning, and zero-shot OOD forecasting with compatible neural operators. The new experiments provide additional support without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds physical explanations for high-frequency content in SST and SSE and interprets parameter-based partitioning as producing more distinct trajectories than time-only grouping. It also explains irregular-grid applicability and the need to omit the uniform-grid FFT loss. The conclusion nevertheless retains irregular grids as future work.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a public-code URL in the abstract and documents the Airfoil adaptation and SSE data resolution and split. Existing hardware, optimizer, loss weights, and baseline hyperparameters are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's actual availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Brunton et al. (2016), Guimarães et al. (2020), and Xu et al. (2025). Appendix B connects the approach more explicitly to sparse equation discovery and operator approximation. The existing related-work discussion is largely retained and moved from Appendix B to C.

P1.justification: Changes include localized rewrites of the real-world evaluation and partition discussion, added appendix subsections, wording corrections, acknowledgements, and publication-header and corresponding-author edits. The introduction, main method narrative, and overall document organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 8, and 17 and Figures 4, 15, and 16, and expands the partition table. Existing figures are retained unchanged. Other visual changes mainly involve table and figure relocation, reflow, and renumbering rather than a broad redesign.

improvement.justification: The SSE and irregular-grid Airfoil evaluations strengthen applicability evidence, while the expanded frequency-loss and partition ablations better support component choices. The code pointer also improves reproducibility information. These are useful extensions to an already extensive empirical study. The theoretical addition remains an approximation argument, and the conclusion's unchanged treatment of irregular grids as future work introduces a minor inconsistency.
